title: Pigeonhole: infinite index sets of pairwise close sets
statement: Let n ∈ ℕ and F_k ⊆ ℝⁿ (k ∈ ℕ) be sets such that for every R > 0 and θ > 0 there is a finite S ⊆ ℕ such that every k has some i ∈ S with L((F_k Δ F_i) ∩ B_R(0)) < θ. Then for every r ∈ ℕ and every infinite I ⊆ ℕ there is an infinite J ⊆ I with L((F_j Δ F_l) ∩ B_{r+1}(0)) ≤ 2^{−r} for all j, l ∈ J.
lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (Fs : ℕ → Set (Euclid n)), (∀ R : ℝ, 0 < R → ∀ θ : ℝ, 0 < θ → ∃ S : Finset ℕ, ∀ k, ∃ i ∈ S, volume (symmDiff (Fs k) (Fs i) ∩ ball (0 : Euclid n) R) < ENNReal.ofReal θ) → ∀ (r : ℕ) (I : Set ℕ), I.Infinite → ∃ J ⊆ I, J.Infinite ∧ ∀ j ∈ J, ∀ l ∈ J, volume (symmDiff (Fs j) (Fs l) ∩ ball (0 : Euclid n) ((r : ℝ) + 1)) ≤ (2⁻¹ : ℝ≥0∞) ^ r
